acceptance_checks.description: For the clean demo drop, ow_tp.silver.custbill_records holds exactly 100 rows for ns=demo and every (account_id, record_type, currency, amount, billing_date) tuple matches the golden .psv rows to the cent.
amount is DECIMAL(12,2) via implied-decimal conversion; billing_date is DATE via strict validation — no string surgery survives into silver.
The copybook trailer record count is enforced: a file whose parsed row count differs from its trailer count is rejected whole to rescue, not partially loaded.
Records failing validation land in ow_tp.silver.custbill_rescue with file_name, raw_line, reject_reason; nothing is silently dropped and nothing invalid reaches custbill_records.
No orphaned temp state on failure; reruns of the same file are idempotent (no duplicate rows).

planted_anomalies.description: Parent plants a record with billing_date 20261332 during live validation; it must appear in custbill_rescue with a date reject_reason and not in custbill_records.
Parent plants a record with a non-numeric implied-decimal amount field; must be quarantined to rescue.
Parent plants a file whose trailer count disagrees with its record count; the whole file must be rejected to rescue, zero rows in custbill_records.

encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Input files are read as bytes; fixed-width slicing operates on byte offsets exactly as the legacy cut/sed/awk chain does. Decoding to text happens per-field after slicing.
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: a field containing bytes outside printable ASCII is a validation failure routed to rescue, never a job crash

malformed_record_policy.details: Fixed-width input has no delimiters: a line whose length differs from copybook CBCUST01 is malformed and goes to rescue. NULL/blank mandatory fields (account, amount, date, currency, type) must never fail open into a plausible-looking silver row — they go to rescue with the reason.

empty_input_semantics.details: No unprocessed bronze files means silver is left untouched and the run exits success; prior output is never truncated or rewritten (legacy: parser exits quietly when incoming/ is empty).
